title: Bekhorot 13
description: The close of chapter one, on when a firstborn donkey is redeemed and which mitzva takes precedence over which, and the opening of chapter two, on a firstborn shared with a gentile and how a Jew and a gentile acquire from each other: with money or by pulling.

a1.he: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו.

a2.he: מֵתִיב רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מִצְוָתוֹ כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — אוֹ פּוֹדֵהוּ אוֹ עוֹרְפוֹ. מַאי לָאו מִצְוָה לְשַׁהוֹתוֹ כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם? לָא, מִצְוָה לִפְדּוֹתוֹ כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.

a3.he: אִי הָכִי, ״מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ אוֹ פּוֹדֵהוּ אוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּמַקֵּשׁי, הָא רַבָּנַן דְּלָא מַקְּשִׁי.

a4.he: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא רָצָה לִפְדּוֹתוֹ — עוֹרְפוֹ מֵאֲחוֹרָיו וְקוֹבְרוֹ. מִצְוַת הַפְּדִיָּיה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת עֲרִיפָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִם לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ״.

a5.he: מִצְוַת יְעִידָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת הַפְּדִיָּיה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְעָדָהּ וְהֶפְדָּהּ״.

a6.he: מִצְוַת הַיִּיבּוּם קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְכַּוְּונִין לְשֵׁם מִצְוָה, וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוְּונִין לְשֵׁם מִצְוָה, אָמְרוּ: מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת יִבּוּם.

a7.he: מִצְוַת הַגְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן, הוּא קוֹדֵם לְכׇל אָדָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל וְנִמְכַּר בְּעֶרְכֶּךָ״.

a9.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי, וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי, וְהַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף לוֹ, וְהַמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ, וְהַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ בְּקַבָּלָה — פָּטוּר מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״, אֲבָל לֹא בַּאֲחֵרִים.

a10.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם חַיָּיבִים, שֶׁלֹּא נִפְטְרוּ מִבְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, אֶלָּא מִפִּדְיוֹן הַבֵּן וּמִפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר.

a11.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי אִירְיָא דְּתָנֵי עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ בְּרֵישָׁא, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ? לִיתְנֵי בְּרֵישָׁא עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ, דִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף הוּא, וַהֲדַר לִיתְנֵי עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ, דִּקְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים הוּא.

a12.he: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, אַיְּידֵי דַּחֲבִיבָא לֵיהּ, כִּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּזוּטְרָן מִילֵּיהּ דִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, פָּסֵיק וְשָׁדֵי לַהּ.

a13.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְגוֹי בִּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּדִינֵיהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה, וְחַיֶּיבֶת בִּבְכוֹרָה. וְגוֹי שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּדִינֵיהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה, וּפָטוּר מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.

a14.he: אָמַר מָר: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְגוֹי בְּדִינֵיהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה וְחַיֶּיבֶת בִּבְכוֹרָה.

a15.he: מַאי ״בְּדִינֵיהֶם״? אִי נֵימָא בְּדִינֵיהֶם דְּגוּפֵיהּ, דְּאָתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר: אִם גּוּפֵיהּ קָנֵי לֵיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכֶסֶף, דִּכְתִיב ״לָרֶשֶׁת אֲחוּזָּה״,

a16.he: הִקִּישׁוֹ הַכָּתוּב לַאֲחוּזָּה, מָה אֲחוּזָּה נִקְנֵית בְּכֶסֶף וּבִשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה, אַף עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי נִקְנֶה בְּכֶסֶף. מָמוֹנוֹ — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן הוּא?

a17.he: אִם כֵּן, אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה נָמֵי! וְעוֹד, יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יוֹכִיחַו, דְּגוּפֵיהּ קָנֵי לֵיהּ בְּכֶסֶף, מָמוֹנוֹ בִּמְשִׁיכָה!

a18.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּדִינֵיהֶם שֶׁפָּסְקָה לָהֶם תּוֹרָה, ״אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ״ — מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ הוּא דְּבִמְשִׁיכָה, הָא מִיַּד גּוֹי בְּכֶסֶף.

a19.he: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי — כְּלָל כְּלָל לָא! אָמְרִי: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא — אִם גּוּפוֹ קוֹנֶה, מָמוֹנוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

a20.he: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי — עַד דְּאִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי! אָמְרִי: וְלָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא? גּוּפוֹ בְּאַחַת, מָמוֹנוֹ בִּשְׁתַּיִם?! וְאֵימָא: אוֹ בְּהָא אוֹ בְּהָא, דּוּמְיָא דַּ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״.

a21.he: מָה ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״ בַּחֲדָא, אַף גּוֹי נָמֵי בַּחֲדָא.

a22.he: אָמַר מָר: וְגוֹי שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּדִינֵיהֶן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה, וּפָטוּר מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה. מַאי בְּדִינֵיהֶן? אִילֵּימָא בְּדִינֵיהֶן דְּגוּפֵיהּ, מִשּׁוּם דְּאָתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר: אִם גּוּפוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָנֵי לֵיהּ בְּכֶסֶף, דִּכְתִיב ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, מָמוֹנוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

a23.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יוֹכִיחַו, דְּגוּפוֹ קָנֵי בְּכֶסֶף, מָמוֹנוֹ בִּמְשִׁיכָה! אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּדִינֵיהֶם שֶׁפָּסְקָה לָהֶם תּוֹרָה, ״וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ״ — לַעֲמִיתֶךָ בִּמְשִׁיכָה, הָא לְגוֹי בְּכֶסֶף.

a24.he: וְאֵימָא: לְגוֹי כְּלָל כְּלָל לָא! אָמְרִי: לָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא? אִם גּוּפוֹ קָנָה, מָמוֹנוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

a25.he: אֵימָא: לְגוֹי עַד דְּאִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי! לָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא? גּוּפוֹ בְּאֶחָד, מָמוֹנוֹ בִּשְׁתַּיִם?!

a26.he: וְאֵימָא: אוֹ בְּהָא אוֹ בְּהָא, דּוּמְיָא דַּ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״;

b1.he: מָה ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״ בְּאַחַת, אַף גּוֹי נָמֵי בְּאַחַת.

b2.he: אָמְרִי: וּלְאָמֵימָר דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיכָה בְּגוֹי קוֹנָה, הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה מָעוֹת קוֹנוֹת, מְשִׁיכָה לֹא, אַהֲנִי ״לַעֲמִיתֶךָ״ — לַעֲמִיתֶךָ בְּכֶסֶף, לְגוֹי בִּמְשִׁיכָה.

b3.he: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר: מְשִׁיכָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת מִן הַתּוֹרָה, לַעֲמִיתֶךָ בִּמְשִׁיכָה, וּלְגוֹי בִּמְשִׁיכָה, ״לַעֲמִיתֶךָ״ לְמָה לִי?

b4.he: אָמְרִי: לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אַתָּה מַחְזִיר אוֹנָאָה, וְאִי אַתָּה מַחֲזִיר אוֹנָאָה לְגוֹי. לְגוֹי — מֵ״אַל תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו״ נָפְקָא!

b5.he: חַד בְּגוֹי, וְחַד בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, וּצְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא חַד — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: לְגוֹי הוּא דְּאֵין לוֹ אוֹנָאָה, אֲבָל הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יֵשׁ לוֹ אוֹנָאָה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b6.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵילוֹ אָסוּר — הַיְינוּ דְּאִצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְמִישְׁרֵי אוֹנָאָה, אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵילוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹי מוּתָּר, אוֹנָאָה מִיבַּעְיָא? אָמְרִי: אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵילוֹ מוּתָּר — עַל כּוּרְחָיךְ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.

b7.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַלּוֹקֵחַ גְּרוּטָאוֹת מִן הַגּוֹיִם, וּמָצָא בָּהֶן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן מָעוֹת מָשַׁךְ — יַחֲזִיר, וְאִם מִשֶּׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת מָשַׁךְ — יוֹלִיךְ הֲנָאָה לְיָם הַמֶּלַח.

b8.he: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מָעוֹת קוֹנוֹת, מְשִׁיכָה לְמָה לִּי? הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. אִי הָכִי, מָעוֹת לְמָה לִי? הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת, אִי מָשֵׁיךְ — אִין, וְאִי לָא — לָא.

b9.he: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רֵישָׁא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא מִקָּח טָעוּת. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: רֵישָׁא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא מִקָּח טָעוּת, סֵיפָא לֵיכָּא מִקָּח טָעוּת?

b10.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא מִקָּח טָעוּת, רֵישָׁא דְּלָא יָהֵיב זוּזֵי — לָא מִיחְזֵי כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל, סֵיפָא דְּיָהֵיב זוּזֵי — מִיחְזֵי כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל.

b11.he: וְאַבַּיֵּי אָמַר לָךְ: רֵישָׁא מִקָּח טָעוּת, דְּלָא יָדַע, דְּהָא לָא יְהַיב לֵיהּ זוּזֵי. סֵיפָא לָאו מִקָּח טָעוּת הוּא, דְּכֵיוָן דִּיהַיב זוּזֵי, כִּי קָא מָשֵׁיךְ — אִיבְּעִי לְעַיּוֹנֵי וַהֲדַר מִימְשָׁךְ.

b12.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִדְּרֵישָׁא מְשִׁיכָה אֵינָהּ קוֹנָה, סֵיפָא נָמֵי מְשִׁיכָה אֵינָהּ קוֹנָה, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״מָשַׁךְ״, תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי ״מָשַׁךְ״.

b13.he: רָבִינָא אָמַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא מְשִׁיכָה קוֹנָה, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי מְשִׁיכָה קוֹנָה, וְרֵישָׁא הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִם לֹא נָתַן וְלֹא מָשַׁךְ — יַחְזוֹר. מַאי יַחְזוֹר? יַחְזוֹר בִּדְבָרִים.

b14.he: קָסָבַר: דְּבָרִים יֵשׁ בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם מְחוּסְּרֵי אֲמָנָה, וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי — יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, דְּקָיְימִי בְּדִבּוּרַיְיהוּ, אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִגּוֹיִם, דְּאִינְהוּ לָא קָיְימִי בְּדִבּוּרַיְיהוּ — לָא.

messages.text: Continued from 12b: one baraita taught that a firstborn donkey is redeemed immediately, another that its laws do not apply before thirty days. Rav Naḥman explained that if one redeemed it immediately it is redeemed, though it should be redeemed only after thirty days ab initio.

The mitzva of redeeming a firstborn donkey takes effect immediately after it is born, as is stated in the first baraita. The second baraita, which states that it applies only after thirty days, means to say that until that time, one does not transgress a prohibition if he has not yet performed the redemption. After thirty days, though, one transgresses a prohibition if he still has not redeemed his firstborn donkey.

notes.he: לעולם מצות פדיון לאלתר והאי דקתני אין בערכין ופטר חמור פחות משלשים שאינו עובר עליו עד שלשים יום מכאן ואילך עובר:
notes.en: Rav Sheshet says: actually the mitzva of redemption is immediate. And that which it teaches, “Valuations and a firstborn donkey do not apply to less than thirty [days],” means that one does not transgress over it until thirty days; from then on, one transgresses.

notes.he: מאי ופדיון פטר חמור לאלתר לומר שאם פדאו קודם ל' אינו עובר עליו אע"ג דפדאו שלא בזמן מצותו:
notes.en: Rav Sheshet says: what [does] “and redeeming a firstborn donkey immediately” [mean]? To say that if he redeemed it before thirty [days], he does not transgress over it, even though he redeemed it not at the time of its mitzva.

messages.text: The mitzva of a firstborn donkey applies throughout the period of thirty days from its birth; from that point forward he must either redeem it immediately or break its neck.
messages.lead: Rami bar Ḥama raises an objection to Rav Sheshet from a baraita:
messages.quote: one does not transgress a prohibition

messages.text: What, does it not mean that there is a mitzva to wait to redeem it until all thirty days have passed?

notes.he: כרב נחמן וקשיא לרב ששת:
notes.en: What, does it not mean a mitzva to keep it [unredeemed]: in accordance with Rav Naḥman, and this is difficult for Rav Sheshet.

notes.he: מאי מצותו כל ל' דקאמר לאו מצוה לשהותו כל שלשים קודם שיפדנו אלמא דאם פדאו קודם עובר עליו:
notes.en: What, does “its mitzva is throughout thirty” not mean that it is a mitzva to keep it for all thirty [days] before he redeems it? Evidently, if he redeemed it earlier, he transgresses over it.

messages.text: No, it means that there is a mitzva to redeem it throughout the period of thirty days, and after that point one has transgressed a prohibition.

notes.he: דמלאלתר עד שלשים הוי זמן פדייה ומכאן ואילך עובר:
notes.en: A mitzva to redeem it: from immediately until thirty [days] is the time of redemption, and from then on one transgresses.

notes.he: לא מצוה לפדותו כל שלשים קאמר דבתוך ל' עד ל' הוי זמן פדייתו ואם לא פדאו עד ל':
notes.en: No: it means it is a mitzva to redeem it throughout thirty [days], for within thirty, up to thirty, is the time of its redemption, and if he did not redeem it by thirty,

messages.text: If so, it should have stated: From that point forward, either he redeems it or he transgresses a prohibition, rather than stating: From that point forward he must either redeem it or break its neck.
messages.quote: from that point forward he must either redeem it immediately or break its neck

notes.dh: עובר עליו מיכן ואילך אי הכי
notes.he: כיון דמוקמת דמצוה לפדותו כל ל'. האי דקתני מיכן ואילך (מל' ואילך) או פודהו או עורפו. מיכן ואילך או עורפו או עובר עליו מיבעי ליה משום דכבר עבר זמן פדייתו אלא מדתני או פודהו או עורפו ש"מ משום הכי או פודהו דמיכן ואילך הוי זמן פדייתו אלמא דמצוה לשהותו וליתא לדרב ששת דאמר לומר שאינו עובר עליו ולטעמיך קשיא אהדדי:
notes.en: he transgresses over it from then on. If so: since you establish that it is a mitzva to redeem it throughout thirty [days], [then] where it teaches “from then on (from thirty onward) either he redeems it or breaks its neck,” [it should have said] “from then on either he breaks its neck or he transgresses over it,” since the time of its redemption has already passed. [A note in the printed edition: Rabbeinu Gershom’s text of the Gemara reads “If so, from then on either he breaks its neck or he transgresses over it,” where ours reads “either he redeems it or he transgresses,” and he explains that according to Rav Sheshet there is no remedy by redemption at all after thirty days.] Rather, since it teaches “either he redeems it or breaks its neck,” learn from this that it says “either he redeems it” because from then on is the time of its redemption. Evidently it is a mitzva to keep it, and Rav Sheshet’s explanation, “to say that he does not transgress over it,” does not hold; and by your reasoning, [the baraitot] contradict each other.

messages.text: Rather, the contradiction between the two baraitot is not difficult, as this baraita, which states that the redemption is performed after thirty days, is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who compares the redemption of a firstborn donkey to the redemption of a woman’s firstborn son, where it is stated: “From a month old shall you redeem them” (Numbers 18:16).

verse.he: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verse.en: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.

notes.he: לעולם מצוה לשהותו ואפי' הכי כרב נחמן לא מתריצנא ולא קשיא הא דקתני שלשים יום מצוה לשהותו:
notes.en: Rather, Rava says: actually it is a mitzva to keep it [for thirty days], and even so I do not resolve it as Rav Naḥman did. And there is no difficulty: this [baraita], which teaches that for thirty days it is a mitzva to keep it,

notes.he: בכור בהמה טמאה לבכור אדם:
notes.en: is Rabbi Eliezer, who compares: the firstborn of a non-kosher animal to the firstborn of a person.

notes.he: אלא אמר רבא לא קשיא הא דתני ובפדיון הבן ובפטר חמור פחות מל' היינו ר' אליעזר דמקיש בכור בהמה טמאה לבכור אדם דכתיב אך פדה תפדה וגו' והא דתני ופדיון פטר חמור לאלתר היינו רבנן דלא מקשי:
notes.en: Rather, Rava says: it is not difficult. This which teaches “and with redemption of the son and a firstborn donkey, [not] less than thirty” is Rabbi Eliezer, who compares the firstborn of a non-kosher animal to the firstborn of a person, as it is written, “But you shall surely redeem,” etc. (Numbers 18:15); and this which teaches “and redeeming a firstborn donkey immediately” is the Rabbis, who do not compare.

messages.text: That baraita, which states that one must perform the mitzva immediately, is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who do not compare the two mitzvot of redemption.

notes.he: דקתני לאלתר רבנן היא דמתניתין דלא מקשו:
notes.en: And that: which teaches “immediately,” is the Rabbis of our mishna, who do not compare.

messages.text: Mishna
If one did not wish to redeem the firstborn donkey, he breaks its neck from behind and buries it.
The mitzva of redeeming the firstborn donkey takes precedence over the mitzva of breaking the neck, as it is stated: “If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck” (Exodus 13:13).

verse.he: וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם־לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: But every firstling donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you must redeem every male first-born among your children.

messages.text: The mitzva of designating a Hebrew maidservant to be betrothed to her master takes precedence over the mitzva of redeeming the maidservant from her master with money, as it is stated: “If she does not please her master, who has not betrothed her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed” (Exodus 21:8).
messages.lead: The mishna proceeds to enumerate other mitzvot in which one option takes precedence over another.

verse.he: אִם־רָעָה בְּעֵינֵי אֲדֹנֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) יְעָדָהּ וְהֶפְדָּהּ לְעַם נׇכְרִי לֹא־יִמְשֹׁל לְמׇכְרָהּ בְּבִגְדוֹ־בָהּ׃
verse.en: If she proves to be displeasing to her master, who designated her for himself, he must let her be redeemed; he shall not have the right to sell her to outsiders, since he broke faith with her.

notes.he: באמה העבריה שייעדנה אדון לאשה:
notes.en: Mishna. The mitzva of designation: with a Hebrew maidservant, whom the master designates as a wife.

notes.he: שהיא פודה עצמה:
notes.en: Takes precedence over the mitzva of redemption: where she redeems herself.

notes.he: אם יעדה זה מוטב:
notes.en: “Who has not designated her, then he shall let her be redeemed”: [implying that] if he designated her, that is better.

messages.text: The mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence over the mitzva of ḥalitza, which dissolves the levirate bond, as it is stated: “And if the man does not wish to take his brother’s wife” (Deuteronomy 25:7).

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יַחְפֹּץ הָאִישׁ לָקַחַת אֶת־יְבִמְתּוֹ וְעָלְתָה יְבִמְתּוֹ הַשַּׁעְרָה אֶל־הַזְּקֵנִים וְאָמְרָה מֵאֵן יְבָמִי לְהָקִים לְאָחִיו שֵׁם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא אָבָה יַבְּמִי׃
verse.en: But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, his brother’s widow shall appear before the elders in the gate and declare, “My husband’s brother refuses to establish a name in Israel for his brother; he will not perform the duty of a levir.”

messages.text: This was the case initially, when people would intend that their performance of levirate marriage be for the sake of the mitzva. But now that they do not intend that their performance of levirate marriage be for the sake of the mitzva, but rather for reasons such as the beauty of the yevama or for financial gain, the Sages said that the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence over the mitzva of levirate marriage.

notes.he: שהמייבם את יבמתו שלא לשם מצוה פוגע באיסור אשת אח:
notes.en: Now the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence: for one who takes his yevama in levirate marriage not for the sake of the mitzva encounters the prohibition of a brother’s wife.

notes.he: מה שפי' רבינו חננאל פי' פרק החולץ (יבמות דף לט:):
notes.en: The mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence: what Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained is explained in chapter HaḤoletz (Yevamot 39b).

notes.he: לבנות בית אחיו:
notes.en: For the sake of the mitzva: to build up his brother’s house.

notes.he: כשהיו אנשים כשרים ועכשיו שאין מתכוונין לשם מצוה. אלא לשם בעילה:
notes.en: Initially: when people were upright. And now, that they do not intend it for the sake of the mitzva, but for the sake of intercourse.

notes.he: דכיון דלא בעיל לשם מצוה הוי כפוגע בערוה:
notes.en: They said the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence: for since he does not have intercourse for the sake of the mitzva, it is as though he encounters a forbidden relation.

messages.text: With regard to a non-kosher animal that was consecrated to the Temple, the mitzva of redemption by the owner who consecrated it takes precedence over redemption by any other person, as it is stated: “And if it is of a non-kosher animal…and if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:27).

verse.he: וְאִם בַּבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁתוֹ עָלָיו וְאִם־לֹא יִגָּאֵל וְנִמְכַּר בְּעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if it is of impure animals, it may be ransomed at its assessment, with one-fifth added; if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessment.

notes.he: במתפיס בהמה טמאה לבדק הבית מצות פדייתה באדון קודם לכל אדם:
notes.en: With the owner: one who consecrates a non-kosher animal for the upkeep of the Temple: the mitzva of redeeming it falls on the owner before anyone else.

notes.dh: מצות גאולה קודמת באדון שנאמר ואם לא יגאל
notes.he: בערכין פרק המקדיש שדהו (ערכין דף כז.) מפ' טעם אחר דבעלים קודמין לפי שמוסיפין חומש והתם פריך לה ומשני:
notes.en: The mitzva of redemption takes precedence with the owner, as it is stated, “And if it is not redeemed”: In Arakhin, chapter HaMakdish Sadeihu (Arakhin 27a), it gives a different reason why the owners take precedence: because they add a fifth. And there it raises a difficulty against this and resolves it.

notes.he: מצות גאולת בהמה טמאה באדון קודם לגאולת כל אדם משום דבעלים מוסיפין חומש כשגואלין אותה. ושאר כל אדם הגואל אותה אין מוסיפין חומש דכתיב ואם בבהמה הטמאה ופדה בערכך ויסף חמישיתו עליו ואם לא גאל (באדם) [בבעלים] נמכר בערכך לכל אדם:
notes.en: The mitzva of redeeming a non-kosher animal by the owner takes precedence over redemption by anyone else, because the owners add a fifth when they redeem it, while anyone else who redeems it does not add a fifth, as it is written: “And if it is of a non-kosher animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation and shall add a fifth part of it to it; and if it is not redeemed” by the owner, “it shall be sold according to your valuation” to anyone.

notes.he: הדרן עלך הלוקח עובר חמורו
notes.en: We will return to you, HaLoke’aḥ Ubar Ḥamoro [the end of chapter 1].

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך הלוקח עובר חמורו · Hadran alakh HaLoke’aḥ Ubar Ḥamoro: we will return to you, chapter 1, “One Who Purchases the Fetus of His Donkey.”
Chapter 2 · הלוקח עובר פרתו · HaLoke’aḥ Ubar Parato: the firstborn of a kosher animal bought from, sold to or shared with a gentile.
Mishna
With regard to one who purchases the fetus of a cow that belongs to a gentile; one who sells the fetus of his cow to a gentile, even though one is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile;

notes.he: מתני' הלוקח עובר פרתו:
notes.en: Mishna. One who purchases the fetus of his cow. [A heading only.]

notes.he: למכור לעובד כוכבים בהמה:
notes.en: Even though he is not permitted: to sell an animal to a gentile.

notes.he: הלוקח:
notes.en: One who purchases. [A heading only, with no comment.]

messages.text: one who enters into a partnership with a gentile with regard to a cow or its fetus; one who receives a cow from a gentile to tend to it in exchange for partnership in its offspring; and one who gives his cow to a gentile in receivership, so that the gentile owns a share of the cow’s offspring;

in all of these cases, one is exempt from the obligation of redeeming the firstborn offspring, as it is stated: “I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal” (Numbers 3:13), indicating that the mitzva is incumbent upon the Jewish people, but not upon others. If the firstborn belongs even partially to a gentile, the sanctity of firstborn does not apply to it.

verse.he: כִּי לִי כׇּל־בְּכוֹר בְּיוֹם הַכֹּתִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הִקְדַּשְׁתִּי לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה לִי יִהְיוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃ {פ}
verse.en: For every such first-born is Mine: at the time that I smote every [male] first-born in the land of Egypt, I consecrated every first-born in Israel, human and animal, to Myself, to be Mine, GOD’s.

messages.text: The priests and the Levites are obligated in the mitzva, i.e., their animals have firstborn sanctity, as they were not exempted from the mitzva of the male firstborn of a kosher animal; rather, they were exempted only from redemption of the firstborn son and from the redemption of the firstborn donkey.

notes.dh: לא נפטרו אלא מפדיון הבן ופטר חמור
notes.he: כדאמר בפרקין דלעיל אך פדה תפדה את בכור האדם ואת בכור הבהמה הטמאה את שישנו בבכור אדם ישנו בבכור בהמה טמאה כו' אלמא דלא נפטרו אלא מאלו ב' דינין:
notes.en: They were exempted only from redemption of the son and the firstborn donkey: as it says in the previous chapter, “But you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal”: whoever is [subject] to the firstborn of man is [subject] to the firstborn of a non-kosher animal, etc. Evidently they were exempted only from these two laws.

messages.text: Gemara
Why does the tanna specifically teach the halakhot of the fetus of his donkey first, and only then teach the halakhot of the fetus of his cow?
messages.lead: The first chapter of this tractate began with the halakhot pertaining to a firstborn donkey.
messages.quote: one who purchases the fetus of a cow

messages.text: Let him first teach the halakhot of the fetus of his cow, as it is a case of inherent sanctity, i.e., the animal cannot be redeemed and is sacrificed upon the altar, and let him then teach the halakhot of the fetus of his donkey, as it is a case of sanctity that inheres in its value.

notes.he: דאינו בר פדייה:
notes.en: Inherent sanctity: for it cannot be redeemed.

messages.text: If you wish, say that the halakhot of a firstborn donkey were taught first since they are dear to the tanna, in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina (5b) that donkeys helped the Jews when they departed from Egypt, as the Jews loaded their gold and silver on donkeys.
messages.lead: They said in the West, Eretz Yisrael:

notes.he: בפ' קמא (לעיל בכורות ה:) מה נשתנו פטרי חמורים מפטרי סוסים וגמלים כו':
notes.en: Gemara. In accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina: in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 5b): “In what way are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels,” etc.

notes.he: איידי דחביבא ליה כר' חנינא דאמ' [לעיל] שהרי סייעו את ישראל וכו':
notes.en: Because it is dear to him, in accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina, who said [above]: for they assisted Israel, etc.

messages.text: And if you wish, say that these halakhot were taught first since the matters pertaining to a non-kosher animal are relatively few, and therefore the tanna completes its treatment and sets it aside.

notes.he: דלא מיירי בפטר חמור אלא פרקא קמא וכולה מסכתא איירי בבכור בהמה טהורה:
notes.en: Because its matters are few: for the firstborn donkey is discussed only in the first chapter, while the whole rest of the tractate discusses the firstborn of a kosher animal.

notes.he: איידי דזוטרן מילתא (דליכא ב') [דלא מיירי ביה] אלא בפרק ראשון אבל כולה מסכתא מיירי בבכור בהמה טהורה:
notes.en: Because its matters are few: for it is discussed only in the first chapter, but the whole tractate discusses the firstborn of a kosher animal.

messages.text: In the case of a Jew who gave money to a gentile to buy the gentile’s animal from him according to their laws, as explained further on, even though the Jew did not pull the animal in the manner of a formal acquisition, as required by halakha, he has legally acquired it, and the Jewish owner is obligated to give the animal’s firstborn offspring to a priest.
messages.lead: § With regard to the mishna’s discussion of sales involving Jews and gentiles, Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani says that Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:

notes.he: בעדרו:
notes.en: With regard to his animal: [that is,] his herd.

notes.he: דיינינן ליה בדיניהן ולקמן מפרש מאי היא:
notes.en: According to their laws: we judge him according to their laws, and below it explains what that is.

notes.he: ואע"ג דשמעינן קנה איצטריך לאשמועינן דחייבת בבכורה דלא תימא קנה מספק או מדרבנן קמ"ל דקנה קנין גמור:
notes.en: He has acquired, and it is obligated in the firstborn: even though we already know that he has acquired, it needed to teach us that it is obligated in the firstborn, so that you should not say he acquired it only out of doubt or by rabbinic law. It teaches us that he acquires it with a complete acquisition.

notes.he: כלומ' כל סחורה שיש יד עובד כוכבים באמצע בעי למיזל אחר דינו ואזלינן בתר דיניהן ובדיניהן מעות קונות:
notes.en: According to their laws: that is, any trade where a gentile’s hand is in the middle must follow his law; we follow their laws, and in their laws money acquires.

messages.text: And in the case of a gentile who gave money to a Jew to buy the Jew’s animal from him according to their laws, even though the gentile did not pull the animal he has acquired it, and the Jew is therefore exempt from giving the animal’s firstborn offspring to a priest.

The Master said: In the case of a Jew who gave money to a gentile to buy the gentile’s animal from him according to their laws, even though he did not pull the animal he has legally acquired it, and the Jew is obligated to give the animal’s firstborn offspring to a priest.
messages.quote: a Jew who gave money to a gentile to buy the gentile’s animal from him according to their laws

messages.text: What is meant by: According to their laws?

If we say that it is referring to the laws relating to the purchase of a gentile’s person as a slave, i.e., the halakhot of purchasing gentiles themselves rather than the methods by which gentiles can acquire property, this must be based on the assumption that the halakha with regard to the purchase of a gentile’s animal is derived by the following a fortiori inference: If a gentile’s person is acquired by a Jew as a Canaanite slave through payment of money, as it is written: “And you may make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for an ancestral possession” (Leviticus 25:46), the same halakha should apply to acquiring a gentile’s property.

verse.he: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם לָרֶשֶׁת אֲחֻזָּה לְעֹלָם בָּהֶם תַּעֲבֹדוּ וּבְאַחֵיכֶם בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו לֹא־תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ׃ {ס}
verse.en: you may keep them as a possession for your children after you, for them to inherit as property for all time. Such you may treat as slaves. But as for your Israelite kin, no one shall rule ruthlessly over another.

notes.he: דעובד כוכבים דנקנה לישראל בכסף דהקישו הכתוב לאחוזה דכתיב והתנחלתם וגו' מה אחוזה נקנית בכסף בשטר ובחזקה אף עבד כנעני:
notes.en: If we say according to the laws of his person: of a gentile, who is acquired by a Jew with money, since the verse compared him to an ancestral possession, as it is written, “And you may make them an inheritance,” etc.: just as an ancestral possession is acquired with money, a document and taking possession, so too a Canaanite slave.

messages.text: The verse thereby compares a gentile slave to an ancestral possession, i.e., land: Just as an ancestral possession is acquired by the transfer of money, or with a bill of sale, or through taking possession, so too, a Canaanite slave is acquired by the transfer of money. If this is the halakha with regard to a gentile’s person, is it not all the more so reasonable that a gentile’s property is acquired through the transfer of money?

notes.he: מכי דייש אמיצרי כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כו.):
notes.en: An ancestral possession is acquired with money, with a document and with taking possession: from when he treads on its boundaries, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (26a).

notes.dh: מה אחוזה נקנית בכסף ובשטר ובחזקה
notes.he: פירוש כשקונה מישראל אף עבד כנעני כן כשקונין מישראל אבל בעובד כוכבים לא מסתבר שיועיל שטר לפי שקנין שטר לא שייך בעובד כוכבים כדאמרי' פ' חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נד:) עובד כוכבים מכי מטא זוזי לידיה איסתליק ליה וישראל לא קני עד דמטא שטרא לידיה:
notes.en: Just as an ancestral possession is acquired with money, a document and taking possession: meaning, when one acquires it from a Jew; so too a Canaanite slave, when one acquires him from a Jew. But with a gentile it is not reasonable that a document should be effective, since acquisition by a document does not apply to a gentile, as we say in chapter Ḥezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 54b): a gentile, once the money reaches his hand, has removed himself [from the property], and the Jew does not acquire until the document reaches his hand.

messages.text: If so, then according to halakha it should be possible to acquire a gentile’s property even with a bill of sale or by taking possession, which is not so.

And furthermore, the halakha pertaining to a Jew purchasing goods from a Jew proves that the entire premise of the a fortiori inference is false, as he acquires a Jew’s person with money alone, but he acquires his property only by pulling. It is therefore evident that the ability to acquire one’s person with money does not indicate that his property can be purchased in the same manner.

notes.he: מטלטלין אין נקנין אלא במשיכה במסכת קדושין (דף כו.):
notes.en: And his property by pulling: movable property is acquired only by pulling, [as stated] in tractate Kiddushin (26a).

notes.he: ועוד מכסף מקנתו משמע בין ישראל לעובד כוכבים בין עובד כוכבים לישראל בכסף:
notes.en: And furthermore, “from the money of his purchase” implies [acquisition] with money both [by] a Jew from a gentile and [by] a gentile from a Jew.

notes.he: מיהא לא שמעי' ישראל מישראל יוכיח דגופו קני ליה בכסף כדאמרן מכסף מקנתו וממונו במשיכה:
notes.en: His property, his animal, all the more so: however, we do not accept this, [for] a Jew from a Jew will prove it: his person one acquires with money, as we said, “from the money of his purchase,” and his property by pulling.

messages.text: The term: Their laws, is referring to their laws that the Torah prescribed for their methods of purchase, by stating: “Or buy of your counterpart’s hand” (Leviticus 25:14), which teaches that it is only from the hand of your counterpart, i.e., a Jew, that property is acquired by the formal act of acquisition of pulling. This indicates that acquiring property from the hand of a gentile is accomplished through payment of money.

verse.he: וְכִי־תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ אַל־תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו׃
verse.en: When you sell property to your neighbor, or buy any from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.

notes.he: משמע מיד ליד דהיינו משיכה:
notes.en: “Of your counterpart’s hand”: implies from hand to hand, which is pulling.

notes.dh: מיד עמיתך במשיכה הא מיד עובד כוכבים בכסף
notes.he: וא"ת דלמא הא מיד עובד כוכבים בשטר ובחזקה דחזקה נמי שייכא במטלטלין אם עשה בהן שום תיקון כעין נעל וגדר ופרץ בקרקע י"ל דשני קנייני' הללו הויין מצויין ושייכי זה במוכר וזה בלוקח שזה נותן מעות וזה מושך אצלו החפץ וכן לרבי יוחנן בסמוך דדרשינן איפכא מיד עמיתך בכסף הא לעובד כוכבים במשיכה וא"ת מנלן שהן חשובין קנין כלל דמוקמינן מסברא קנינין דקרא בהני י"ל דאשכחן כסף שקונה במקום אחר בקרקע ובהקדש ומשיכה במציאה והפקר:
notes.en: From the hand of your counterpart by pulling, so from the hand of a gentile with money: And if you say: perhaps [infer that] from the hand of a gentile it is with a document or by taking possession, for taking possession also applies to movable property, if he made some improvement in them, like locking, fencing or breaching [a wall] with land? One can say that these two acquisitions [money and pulling] are common, and they belong one to the seller and one to the buyer: this one gives money and that one draws the object to himself. And so too according to Rabbi Yoḥanan below, where we expound the opposite, “your counterpart” with money, so a gentile by pulling. And if you say: from where do we know that they count as an acquisition at all, such that we establish by reasoning that the acquisitions of the verse are these? One can say that we find money acquiring elsewhere, with land and with consecrated property, and pulling with a found object and with ownerless property.

notes.dh: מיד עמיתך הוא דבמשיכה דכתיב מיד דבר הניתן מיד ליד
notes.he: מיד עובד כוכבים מכסף:
notes.en: “Of your counterpart’s hand”: it is by pulling, for it is written “hand,” a thing given from hand to hand. From the hand of a gentile, with money.

messages.text: But one can say that it should be inferred from the verse that one cannot purchase anything at all from the hand of a gentile.
messages.quote: from the hand of a gentile is accomplished through payment of money

notes.he: עד שתבא לרשותו של ישראל לא קני:
notes.en: Not at all: he does not acquire until it comes into the domain of the Jew.

messages.text: That cannot enter your mind, as there is an a fortiori inference which indicates otherwise: If a Jew can purchase a gentile’s person as a slave, is it not all the more so reasonable that he can purchase a gentile’s property?

notes.he: ואימא דלהכי אתא קרא מיד עמיתך הוא דליקני מיד עובד כוכבים כלל כלל לא דאם רוצה העובד כוכבים לחזור בו יכול לחזור בו. הא ליכא למימר דהשתא גופו קנה בכסף כ"ש ממונו:
notes.en: And say that this is why the verse comes: from the hand of your counterpart he acquires; from the hand of a gentile, not at all, for if the gentile wishes to retract, he can retract. This cannot be said, for if he acquires his person with money, all the more so his property.

messages.text: But one can say that the verse teaches that whereas a Jew’s property is acquired through pulling, property purchased from the hand of a gentile is not acquired until two formal acts of acquisition have been performed, both pulling and payment of money.

notes.he: מיד עמיתך במשיכה גרידא מיד עובד כוכבים עד דאיכא תרתי כסף ומשיכה:
notes.en: And say: from the hand of your counterpart by pulling alone; from the hand of a gentile, not until there are both, money and pulling.

messages.text: Isn’t it indicated otherwise by an a fortiori inference: If his person is acquired through only one act of acquisition, could it be that his property must be acquired through two acts?
But one can say that it is derived from the verse that one can acquire property from a gentile either through this method of pulling or through that method of money.

notes.he: והכי משמע קרא מיד עמיתך הוא דבמשיכה ולא בכסף הא מיד עובד כוכבים באיזה שתרצה ונשמע מיניה דהיכא דמשך ולא נתן מעו' נמי קני:
notes.en: And say either this or that: and the verse would imply: from the hand of your counterpart it is by pulling and not by money, but from the hand of a gentile, by whichever [method] you wish. And we would learn from it that where he pulled and did not give money, he has also acquired.

messages.text: The halakha derived from the phrase “of your counterpart” must be similar to an acquisition from your counterpart:
Just as from the hand of your counterpart it is with one act, with pulling, so too, from the hand of a gentile, it is also with one act, with money.

notes.he: משיכה:
notes.en: Just as your counterpart with one: pulling.

notes.he: בכסף ולא במשיכה דהכי משמע עמיתך במשיכה ולא עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: So too a gentile with one: with money and not by pulling, for this is what it implies: your counterpart by pulling, and not a gentile.

notes.he: דומיא דעמיתך מה עמיתך בחדא במשיכה ולא במעות אף עובד כוכבים בחדא במעות ולא במשיכה. וכדאמרן לעובד כוכבים כלל כלל לא דאינו קונה מישראל לא במשיכה ולא בכסף:
notes.en: Similar to your counterpart: just as your counterpart with one, by pulling and not with money, so a gentile with one, with money and not by pulling. And as we said: to a gentile not at all, that he does not acquire from a Jew either by pulling or with money.

messages.text: The Master said: And a gentile who gave money to a Jew to buy the Jew’s animal from him according to their laws, even though the gentile did not pull the animal he has acquired it, and the Jew is therefore exempt from giving the animal’s firstborn offspring to a priest.
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses the statement of Rabbi Oshaya.
messages.quote: a gentile who gave money to a Jew to buy the Jew’s animal from him according to their laws

messages.text: The Gemara clarifies: What is the meaning of according to their laws? If we say that it means: According to their laws of the person of the Jew himself, i.e., the manner in which he purchases the person of a Jew with money, and it is reasonable to say so, as it may be derived through an a fortiori inference: If a gentile acquires the body of a Jew with money, as it is written in that regard: “From the money of his purchase” (Leviticus 25:51), then with regard to the property of a Jew, is it not all the more so reasonable that the gentile can acquire it with money?

verse.he: אִם־עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים לְפִיהֶן יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ׃
verse.en: If many years remain, [your kin] shall pay back for the redemption in proportion to the purchase price;

notes.he: בעבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים הכתוב מדבר:
notes.en: “From the money of his purchase”: the verse speaks of a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile.

notes.he: אם גופו דישראל קני ליה עובד כוכבים בכסף כו' מדלא פריך הכא אם כן אפי' בשטר וחזקה נמי כדפריך לעיל יש ראיה לפר"ת דמפרש פרק קמא דקדושין (דף יד:) אשכחן עבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים שכל קניינו בכסף כלומר כל קנינו דעובד כוכבים בעבד עברי בכסף כדכתיב (ויקרא כה) מכסף מקנתו ולא בשטר וחזקה כדמוכח הכא ובקונטרס פי' שם דכל דבר קניינו בכסף כדדרשינן הכא מיד עמיתך במשיכה הא מיד עובד כוכבים בכסף וקשה דהאי דרשא לריש לקיש היא והלכה כר' יוחנן וא"ת אכתי עובד כוכבי' קונה ישראל בחזקה כדאמר גיטין (דף לח.) מנין לעובד כוכבים שקונה ישראל בחזקה שנאמר וישב ממנו שבי י"ל דההיא חזקה כשיש מלחמה הוא והוא הדין ממונו כדאמר חולין (דף ס:) עמון ומואב טיהרו בסיחון:
notes.en: (Above) If his person is acquired: if a gentile acquires the person of a Jew with money, etc. From the fact that it does not object here, “If so, even with a document and taking possession too,” as it objected above, there is a proof for the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explains in the first chapter of Kiddushin (14b), “We have found a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, whose entire acquisition is by money”: meaning, a gentile’s entire acquisition of a Hebrew slave is by money, as it is written, “From the money of his purchase” (Leviticus 25:51), and not by a document or taking possession, as is evident here. And Rashi explained there that [a gentile’s acquisition of] every item is by money, as we expound here: “of your counterpart” by pulling, so from a gentile with money. But this is difficult, for this derivation is according to Reish Lakish, and the halakha follows Rabbi Yoḥanan. And if you say: still, a gentile acquires a Jew by taking possession, as it says in Gittin (38a): “From where do we know that a gentile acquires a Jew by taking possession? As it is stated: ‘And took some of them captive’” (Numbers 21:1)? One can say that that taking possession is when there is war, and the same is true of his property, as it says in Ḥullin (60b): Ammon and Moab were purified through Siḥon.

messages.text: This can be rejected, as the acquisition of a Jew from a Jew will prove that the inference is not valid, as the person of a Hebrew slave one acquires with money, while the property of a Jew can be acquired only by pulling.

That which it states, that a gentile purchases an animal with money according to their laws, means: With the acts of acquisition that the Torah prescribed to gentiles, the manner in which they acquire items from Jews, i.e., with money, as it is stated: “And if you sell a sale item to your counterpart” (Leviticus 25:14), from which it may be inferred: To your counterpart, i.e., a Jew, property is acquired by pulling, but property from the hand of a gentile is acquired with money.
But say that the inference should be: To a gentile, not at all, i.e., neither with money nor with pulling can a gentile acquire an item from a Jew.
messages.quote: To your counterpart, i.e., a Jew, property is acquired by pulling

notes.dh: אימא לעובד כוכבים כלל כלל לא קל וחומר אם גופו קני ממונו לא כל שכן
notes.he: וא"ת דלמא בחליפין דהוא מקני ממונו כדדריש בקדושין (דף ח.) מכסף מקנתו בכסף הוא נקנה ואינו נקנה בתורת תבואה וכלים ומאי נינהו חליפין ובעבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים כתיב האי קרא משמע הא שאר כגון מטלטלין קונה עובד כוכבים בחליפין וי"ל דאי לא אשכחן כסף או משיכה בעובד כוכבים לא הוה מוקמינן ליה בחליפין ועי"ל האי דקאמר עובד כוכבים בחדא לאו בחליפין ששוה בעובד כוכבים ובישראל מיירי אלא בקנין חדש כגון כסף או משיכה:
notes.en: Say: to a gentile, not at all. An a fortiori inference: if he acquires his person, is it not all the more so his property: And if you say: perhaps [he acquires] by exchange [ḥalifin], since he acquires his property [that way], as it expounds in Kiddushin (8a): “From the money of his purchase”: he is acquired with money, and he is not acquired by way of grain and vessels; and what are these? Exchange. And this verse is written about a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, which implies that other things, such as movable property, a gentile acquires by exchange? One can say that had we not found money or pulling with a gentile, we would not have established it as exchange. Alternatively, one can say that when it says “a gentile with one,” it is not speaking of exchange, which is the same for a gentile and for a Jew, but of a new acquisition, such as money or pulling.

messages.text: But isn’t it an a fortiori inference to the contrary: If a gentile can purchase a Jew’s person as a slave, then is it not all the more so reasonable that he can purchase the Jew’s property?

notes.he: לגופו דישראל קנה בכסף כ"ש ממונו בהמתו [ע"כ שייך לע"א]:
notes.en: They said: is it not an a fortiori inference? [If] he acquires the person of a Jew with money, all the more so his property, his animal. [The printed edition notes that this belongs to amud a.]

messages.text: Say and infer as follows: To your counterpart you sell with pulling, but to a gentile you do not sell until two formal acts of acquisition have been performed: Pulling and money.
But isn’t it an a fortiori inference to the contrary: If the person of a Jew is acquired with one act of acquisition, is it reasonable that his property is acquired with two acts?
But say that a gentile acquires property from a Jew either with this act of pulling or with that act of paying money.
The acquisition of the gentile must be similar to the acquisition of your counterpart, from which it is derived:

Just as property is acquired from your counterpart through only one act of acquisition, i.e., pulling, so too, property is acquired from a gentile through only one act of acquisition, i.e., payment of money.

And according to the opinion of Ameimar, who says that pulling effects acquisition in the case of a gentile, this works out well if he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says: By Torah law, money effects acquisition, but pulling does not.

notes.he: בפרק בתרא דע"ז (דף עא:):
notes.en: According to Ameimar, who says, etc.: in the last chapter of Avoda Zara (71b).

notes.dh: הניחא אי סבר לה כרבי יוחנן
notes.he: דאמר בפרק הזהב (ב"מ מו:) דבר תורה מעות קונות דכתיב ונתן הכסף וקם לו דגמר הדיוט מהקדש ומשיכה לא קניא איכא למימר דעמיתך אתי למימר מיד עמיתך בכסף ומיד עובד כוכבים במשיכה:
notes.en: This works out well if he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan: who says in chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 46b) that by Torah law money acquires, as it is written, “Then he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him” (Leviticus 27:19), for an ordinary person is derived from consecrated property, and pulling does not acquire. [Then] one can say that “your counterpart” comes to say: from the hand of your counterpart with money, and from the hand of a gentile by pulling.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס דכתיב בהקדש ונתן הכסף וקם לו וגמר הדיוט מהקדש וא"ת לריש לקיש דאמר משיכה מפורשת מן התורה ליגמר שיקנה כסף בהדיוט כמו בהקדש ומשיכה נמי תקני בהקדש כמו בהדיוט ותירץ הרב רבי יהודה בר נתן דמשיכה לא שייכא בהקדש דכל היכא דאיתיה בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה ולהכי שייך טפי כסף מבהדיוט שבהדיוט דאפשר במשיכה לא יהא (אלא) קנין אחר ונראה לר"י דמקרא נפיק ליה שפיר דרשינן מיד עמיתך במשיכה הא מיד עובד כוכבים בכסף ומדעובד כוכבים בחדא ישראל נמי בחדא דשניהם למדין זה על זה דליכא למימר דלא משתעי קרא אלא דעובד כוכבים בהא או בהא וכן ישראל דא"כ היו שוין ואפילו אם תימצי לומר שיקנה חליפין בישראל ולא בעובד כוכבים ולא כדפרישית לעיל מצי למימר דלא משתעי קרא אלא בקנינין הרגילין ומצויין כגון כסף ומשיכה ובהנך למדין ישראל ועובד כוכבים זה מזה ועוד מפרש ר' טעמא דר' יוחנן דמעות קונות מגופיה דקרא דאו קנה מיד עמיתך דסתם קנין דקרא במעות כדכתיב (ירמיהו ל״ב:מ״ד) שדות בכסף יקנו וכתיב מכסף מקנתו (ויקרא כה):
notes.en: By Torah law money acquires: Rashi explained that it is written of consecrated property, “Then he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him,” and an ordinary person is derived from consecrated property. And if you say: according to Reish Lakish, who says pulling is explicit in the Torah, let us derive that money acquires with an ordinary person as with consecrated property, and that pulling too acquires with consecrated property as with an ordinary person? The Rav, Rabbi Yehuda bar Natan, answered that pulling does not apply to consecrated property, for wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One. That is why money fits consecrated property more than an ordinary person: for with an ordinary person, where pulling is possible, there should be no other acquisition. And it seems to the Ri that he derives it well from the verse: we expound “of your counterpart’s hand” by pulling, so from the hand of a gentile with money; and from the fact that a gentile [acquires] with one, a Jew too [acquires] with one, for the two are learned from each other. For one cannot say that the verse speaks only to say that a gentile [acquires] with either this or that, and likewise a Jew, for if so they would be the same. And even if you were to say that exchange acquires with a Jew and not with a gentile, unlike what I explained above, one can say that the verse speaks only of the usual and common acquisitions, such as money and pulling, and with these a Jew and a gentile are learned from each other. And [my] teacher further explains the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan, that money acquires, from the verse itself, “or buy of your counterpart’s hand,” for an unspecified acquisition in Scripture is with money, as it is written, “Fields shall be bought for money” (Jeremiah 32:44), and it is written, “From the money of his purchase” (Leviticus 25:51).

notes.he: בבבא מציעא משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה הניחא אי סבר לה כר' יוחנן דאמר דבר תורה מעות קונות ישראל מישראל ולא משיכה. מתרץ לה הכי לעמיתך בכסף ולעובד כוכבים במשיכה. משום הכי איצטריך למיכתב לעמיתך דעמיתך בכסף ולא לעובד כוכבים ומהפך לו שמעתא דר' יצחק אלא אי סבר לה כריש לקיש כו' א"כ לעמיתך מאי אתא למעוטי כיון דתרווייהו במשיכה:
notes.en: And according to Ameimar, who says in Bava Metzia that pulling acquires with a gentile: this works out well if he holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says that by Torah law money acquires, a Jew from a Jew, and not pulling. He resolves it thus: to your counterpart with money, and to a gentile by pulling. That is why it needed to write “to your counterpart”: your counterpart with money, and not a gentile; and he reverses the teaching of Rabbi Yitzḥak [bar Naḥmani]. But if he holds like Reish Lakish, etc., then what does “to your counterpart” come to exclude, since both are by pulling?

messages.text: If Ameimar accepts Rabbi Yoḥanan’s opinion, then it can be derived from the phrase “of your counterpart” that transactions with your counterpart, i.e., a Jew, are effected through payment of money, whereas transactions with a gentile are effected by pulling.

messages.caption: Two readings of “of your counterpart’s hand”: how a Jew acquires from a Jew, and how acquisition works across a Jew and a gentile.

messages.text: But if Ameimar holds in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish, who says: The act of acquisition of pulling is explicit in the Torah, then the halakha is that transactions with your counterpart are effected by pulling, and transactions with a gentile are also effected by pulling. Accordingly, why do I need the phrase “of your counterpart”?

notes.he: מיד עמיתך משמע מיד ליד:
notes.en: Explicit in the Torah: “of your counterpart’s hand” implies from hand to hand.

messages.text: The phrase “of your counterpart” does not teach a halakha with regard to the method of acquisition. Rather, it is referring to the latter part of the verse: “And if you make a sale to your counterpart, or buy of your counterpart’s hand, a man shall not exploit his brother” (Leviticus 25:14). The verse is derived as follows: You must return the sum of exploitation to your counterpart, but you do not need to return the sum of exploitation to a gentile.
messages.quote: why do I need the phrase “of your counterpart”

verse.he: וְכִי־תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ אַל־תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו׃
verse.en: When you sell property to your neighbor, or buy any from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.

notes.he: דממעט כנעני מדין אונאה דכתיב בסיפיה דקרא קממעטי ליה:
notes.en: They said: to your counterpart: for it excludes a Canaanite [i.e., a gentile] from the law of exploitation, as written at the end of the verse, it excludes him.

messages.text: The exemption from returning the sum of exploitation to a gentile is derived from the latter part of the verse alone: “A man shall not exploit his brother.” A gentile is not included in the category of “his brother.” Accordingly, the phrase “of your counterpart” remains extraneous.
messages.quote: but you do not need to return the sum of exploitation to a gentile

notes.dh: אונאה מאל תונו איש את אחיו נפקא
notes.he: דמשמע אחיו ולא כנעני:
notes.en: Exploitation is derived from “a man shall not exploit his brother”: which implies his brother, and not a Canaanite.

messages.text: One phrase is required to exclude a gentile, and one serves to exclude consecrated property.

notes.dh: חד למעוטי כנעני וחד למעוטי הקדש
notes.he: מאונאה:
notes.en: One to exclude a Canaanite and one to exclude consecrated property: from [the law of] exploitation.

notes.he: שלא תאמר לא תהא כח הדיוט חמור מהקדש קמ"ל לעמיתך ולא להקדש:
notes.en: And one to exclude consecrated property: so that you should not say the power of an ordinary person should not be greater than consecrated property; it teaches us “your counterpart,” and not consecrated property.

messages.text: And both derivations are necessary, as, had the Merciful One written only one exclusionary phrase, I would say: It is with regard to transactions with a gentile that one is not subject to the prohibition of exploitation; but with regard to transactions involving consecrated property, one is subject to the prohibition of exploitation. Therefore, the other derivation teaches us that one is not subject to the prohibition of exploitation with regard to transactions involving consecrated property either.

This works out well according to the one who says that his robbery, i.e., robbing a gentile, is prohibited, as this is the reason that a verse is necessary to permit keeping the sum of the exploitation obtained from a gentile. But if Ameimar holds in accordance with the opinion of the one who says that his robbery is permitted, is it necessary to state that one may keep the sum of the exploitation obtained from a gentile?

notes.he: של כנעני אסור בב"ק בפ' הגוזל בתרא (בבא קמא דף קיג:):
notes.en: According to the one who says his robbery: of a Canaanite is forbidden, in Bava Kamma, the last chapter, HaGozel (Bava Kamma 113b).

notes.he: פ"ה פלוגתא בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיג:) וכולה שמעתא דהתם מוכח דאסור ובהפקעת הלואתו פליגי אבל בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נז.) תניא גזל וגנב וכן יפת תואר ישראל בכנעני מותר ובפ' המקבל (ב"מ דף קיא:) נמי אמר חד למישרי גזילו של כנעני וחד למישרי עושקו גבי רעיך ואחיך וא"ת וגזל הכנעני היכי שרי הכתיב (ויקרא כז) וחשב עם קונהו ובכנעני שהוא תחת ידך משתעי דאי אין תחת ידו מי ציית לפי שנים שעבר היובל י"ל היכא דאיכא חלול השם ודאי אסור וכי שרית היכא דאית ליה לאישתמוטי וגזל ממנו בעלילה או בכמה עניינים:
notes.en: According to the one who says robbing a Canaanite is permitted: Rashi explained that it is a dispute in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 113b). But the whole discussion there shows that it is forbidden, and they disagree about withholding his loan. However, in chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 57a) it is taught: robbery, theft, and likewise a beautiful captive woman, a Jew with a Canaanite is permitted. And in chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 111b) too it says: one [verse] to permit robbing a Canaanite and one to permit withholding his wages, regarding “your fellow” and “your brother.” And if you say: how is robbing a Canaanite permitted? Isn’t it written, “And he shall reckon with his purchaser” (Leviticus 25:50), which speaks of a Canaanite who is under your authority, for if he is not under his authority, who would obey, [reckoning] according to the years [remaining] until the Jubilee? One can say: where there is desecration of God’s name it is certainly forbidden, and where it is permitted is where he has a way to evade it, and he robbed him by a pretext or in various such ways.

notes.he: דעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: His robbery is forbidden: of a gentile.

messages.text: If Ameimar holds in accordance with the opinion of the one who says that his robbery is permitted, perforce he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan that money effects acquisition by Torah law, and therefore the difficulty does not arise.

notes.he: ודאי אי סבר גזילו של כנעני מותר תו לא אתא קרא למישרי אונאה אלא למעטיה מדין קנייה וכיון דאמר עובד כוכבים קנה במשיכה על כרחיך כר' יוחנן סבירא ליה דמכסף קא ממעיט ליה:
notes.en: They said: certainly, if he holds that robbing a Canaanite is permitted, the verse no longer comes to permit exploitation, but to exclude him from the law of acquisition. And since he says that a gentile acquires by pulling, perforce he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, that [the verse] excludes him from [acquiring with] money.

notes.he: אי סבר לה כמאן דאמר גזלו מותר ולא איצטריך לעמיתך לאונאה על כרחיך אמימר כרבי יוחנן ס"ל דאמר דבר תורה מעות קונות והלכך איצטריך לעמיתך דלעמיתך בכסף ולעובד כוכבים במשיכה:
notes.en: If he holds like the one who says his robbery is permitted, and “to your counterpart” is not needed for exploitation, perforce Ameimar holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says by Torah law money acquires; therefore “to your counterpart” is needed: to your counterpart with money, and to a gentile by pulling.

messages.text: § The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion that property is acquired from a gentile by monetary payment.

With regard to one who buys broken vessels [gerutaot] made of gold or silver from the gentiles and finds among them an object of idol worship, if he pulled the object of idol worship, thereby performing an act of acquisition, before he gave the money to the gentile, he may return the object of idol worship to the gentile.

notes.he: חתיכות כסף:
notes.en: Gerutaot: pieces of silver.

notes.he: דמשיכה אינה קונה:
notes.en: He may return: for pulling does not acquire.

notes.he: חתיכות כסף קטנות:
notes.en: Gerutaot: small pieces of silver.

messages.text: But if he pulled it after he gave the money to the gentile, he may not return it. Since the idol’s status was not revoked, he must take it and cast it into the Dead Sea.

notes.he: דעבודת כוכבים ביד ישראל אינה בטילה עולמית:
notes.en: To the Dead Sea: for an object of idol worship in the possession of a Jew can never have its status revoked.

notes.he: דהשתא הוויין שלו ואסור לקיימה ברשותו ואסור לו למוכרה:
notes.en: He takes the benefit to the Dead Sea: for now they are his, and it is forbidden to keep it in his possession, and forbidden for him to sell it.

messages.text: And if you say that payment of money acquires items from gentiles, why do I need pulling in order to effect the Jew’s acquisition of the idol?
messages.quote: if he pulled it after he gave the money to the gentile

notes.he: משיכה למה לי:
notes.en: Why do I need pulling. [A heading only.]

notes.dh: ואי אמרת מעות קונות משיכה למה לי
notes.he: תימה דבפ' בתרא דע"ז (דף עא:) מייתי הך ברייתא למידק איפכא מרישא דקאמר ואי אמרת משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה אמאי יחזיר ואומר ר"י דהמקשה סובר הכא והתם דתרוייהו בעינן בכנעני משיכה ומעות והשתא ניחא ליה הכא והתם רישא וסיפא:
notes.en: And if you say money acquires, why do I need pulling: This is puzzling, for in the last chapter of Avoda Zara (71b) it brings this baraita to infer the opposite from the first clause, saying: and if you say pulling acquires with a gentile, why should he return it? And the Ri says that the questioner holds, both here and there, that with a Canaanite we require both pulling and money, and now, both here and there, the first clause and the latter clause work out well for him.

messages.text: Here we are dealing with a case where the gentile accepted upon himself to have this transaction adjudicated by Jewish law.
If so, why do I need the payment of money in order to effect the Jew’s acquisition of the idol? Pulling alone should be enough, in accordance with halakha.

This is what the baraita means: Even though the Jew gave money to the gentile, the halakha still depends on the act of pulling: If he pulled the broken vessels, yes, he has acquired them, and if not, he has not acquired them.

notes.dh: הכי קאמר אע"פ שנתן מעות אי משך אין אי לא משך לא
notes.he: וא"ת והא איכא מי שפרע יש לומר כשקבל עליו לדון בדיני ישראל ומי שפרע אין זה דין א"נ כמו שמפרש ר"ת בפרק הזהב (ב"מ מז:) דלענין יוקרא וזולא צריך מי שפרע אבל לא במקום שמפסיד לגמרי ואע"ג דבסמוך מפורש משום דברים בעלמא אי הוה בהו משום מחוסרי אמנה היה נאסר משום דמחזי כעבודת כוכבים ביד ישראל ואביי לא חייש למיחזי עבודת כוכבים ביד ישראל ועוד דכאן לא מיחזי כלל כיון דמי שפרע ליכא כדפרישית וליכא נמי משום מחוסרי אמנה בעובד כוכבים טפי מבישראל:
notes.en: This is what it means: even though he gave money, if he pulled, yes; if he did not pull, no: And if you say: but there is [the curse] “He Who exacted payment” [for one who retracts after paying]? One can say: [this is] where he accepted upon himself to be judged by Jewish law, and “He Who exacted payment” is not [part of] the law. Alternatively, as Rabbeinu Tam explains in chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b), “He Who exacted payment” is needed regarding a rise or fall in price, but not where he would lose entirely. And even though just below [Ravina] explains [it as] mere words, [where] if they involved a breach of faith he would be forbidden [to retract], because it would look like idol worship in the possession of a Jew, Abaye is not concerned about the appearance of idol worship in the possession of a Jew. Moreover, here it does not appear so at all, since there is no “He Who exacted payment,” as I explained, and there is also no greater breach of faith with a gentile than with a Jew.

messages.text: If so, then the first clause of the baraita is difficult, as it states: If he pulled the object of idol worship before he gave the money to the gentile, he may return the object of idol worship to the gentile. Evidently, pulling alone does not effect acquisition.
messages.quote: if he pulled the object of idol worship before he gave the money to the gentile, he may return

notes.he: דאמאי יחזיר והא משך והיה [צריך] להוליך לים המלח:
notes.en: If so, the first clause is difficult: for why should he return it? He pulled, and he should have to take it to the Dead Sea.

messages.text: The halakha in the first clause is ruled as it is because there is a mistaken transaction, as the Jew did not wish to purchase the idol.

notes.he: דלא ידע דאית בה עבודת כוכבים הלכך מצי למיהדר ביה:
notes.en: A mistaken transaction: for he did not know that there was an object of idol worship among them; therefore he can retract.

notes.he: דלא ידע דהוה בהו עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: For there is a mistaken transaction: for he did not know that there was idol worship among them.

messages.text: @Abaye You maintain that the halakha of the first clause is ruled as it is because there is a mistaken transaction. Is that to say that in the latter clause there is no mistaken transaction? After all, the Jew does not wish to purchase the idol in either case.
messages.quote: because there is a mistaken transaction

notes.dh: רישא איכא מקח טעות סיפא ליכא מקח טעות
notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: In the first clause there is a mistaken transaction, and in the latter clause there is no mistaken transaction: [said] in astonishment.

messages.text: The purchase in the first clause and the purchase in the latter clause are both a mistaken transaction, but in the case presented in the first clause, where the Jew did not pay him the dinars, it does not appear as though there is an object of idol worship in the possession of a Jew, and so he may return it.

notes.he: ומדינא מצי מהדר ביה נמי בסיפא ומיהו רבנן גזרו כיון דיהיב זוזי והדר שקיל להו מיחזי כמוכר עבודת כוכבים ורישא דלא יהיב זוזי וכי מהדר לה לא מידי שקיל לא מיחזי כעבודת כוכבים ביד ישראל ומשום הכי נקט מתן מעות אע"ג דקיבל עליו לדון בדיני ישראל:
notes.en: The first clause and the latter clause are a mistaken transaction: and by law he could retract in the latter clause too. But the Rabbis decreed [otherwise], since if he gave dinars and then takes them back, it looks as though he is selling an object of idol worship. In the first clause, where he did not give dinars, when he returns it he takes nothing back, so it does not look like idol worship in the possession of a Jew. And that is why it mentions the giving of money, even though [the gentile] accepted upon himself to be judged by Jewish law.

notes.he: ומשיכה קונה שקבל לדון בדיני ישראל:
notes.en: The first clause and the latter clause are a mistaken transaction: and pulling acquires, since he accepted to be judged by Jewish law.

messages.text: By contrast, in the latter clause, where the Jew did pay him the dinars, it appears as though there is an object of idol worship in the possession of a Jew, and therefore he must cast away the object rather than return it.
The first clause involves a mistaken transaction, as he did not know that the idol was included, as he did not give him the dinars and therefore had not yet inspected the property being purchased.

notes.he: דאית בהו עבודת כוכבים דהא לא יהיב זוזי דלימא איבעי לעיוני דסתם תגר לא מעיין עד שעת מתן מעות:
notes.en: For he did not know: that there was idol worship among them, since he had not given the dinars, such that we would say he should have inspected; for an ordinary merchant does not inspect until the time he gives the money.

notes.he: לעולם כדאמינא רישא דאיכא מקח טעות דאע"ג דמשך כיון דאכתי לא יהיב זוזי לא דק אי הוי בהו עבודת כוכבים אי לא הלכך יחזיר:
notes.en: And Abaye would say to you: really, it is as I said: the first clause involves a mistaken transaction, for even though he pulled, since he had not yet given the dinars, he did not check whether there was idol worship among them or not; therefore he returns it.

messages.text: Conversely, the latter clause is not a case of a mistaken transaction, as since he already gave the dinars to the seller, when he came to pull it, he should have inspected the property and then pulled it. Since the Jew did not bother to inspect the property even after paying, the transaction is valid.

notes.he: ומדלא עיין אחולי אחיל והוי משיכתו משיכה גמורה:
notes.en: He should have inspected: and since he did not inspect, he waived [his claim], and his pulling is a complete pulling.

notes.dh: דכיון דיהיב זוזי איבעי ליה לעיוני והדר ממשיך
notes.he: ואף על גב דבשאר מקח טעות לא אמרינן הכי שאני לוקח גרוטאות מיד עובד כוכבים דאיבעי ליה לאסוקי אדעתא טפי שמא יש בהן עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: Since he gave the dinars, he should have inspected and then pulled: Even though with other mistaken transactions we do not say this, one who buys broken vessels from a gentile is different, for he should have been more mindful that perhaps there is idol worship among them.

notes.he: דכיון דיהב זוזי והדר משך עיוני עיין [ומדלא עיין] אחולי אחיל ולא הוי מקח טעות:
notes.en: And the latter clause is not a mistaken transaction: for since he gave the dinars and then pulled, he should have inspected; [and since he did not inspect,] he waived [his claim], and it is not a mistaken transaction.

messages.text: The baraita is in fact discussing a case where the transaction was subject to gentile law, according to which only monetary payment effects acquisition, and as for the aforementioned difficulty raised to the opinion of Rabbi Oshaya from the latter clause: If so, why do I need pulling in order to effect the Jew’s acquisition of the idol; pulling is not in fact required.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites two more interpretations of the baraita.

notes.he: לעולם בשלא קיבל עליו לדון בדיני ישראל ולא קשיא סיפא לר' אושעיא ודקאמרת אי מעות קונות משיכה ל"ל משיכה לאו דוקא דמדרישא משיכה אינה קונה דקתני יחזיר סיפא נמי משיכה אינה קונה:
notes.en: Rav Ashi says: actually [the case is] where he did not accept upon himself to be judged by Jewish law, and the latter clause is not difficult for Rabbi Oshaya. And as for what you said, “If money acquires, why do I need pulling”: pulling is not meant precisely, for from the first clause, pulling does not acquire, as it teaches “he may return,” so in the latter clause too pulling does not acquire.

messages.text: Rather, from the fact that in the first clause, pulling does not effect acquisition, in the latter clause too, pulling does not effect acquisition. But since the first clause taught the word: Pulled, in order to teach that this method is ineffective, the latter clause also taught the word: Pulled, despite the fact that its mention is unnecessary.

notes.dh: רב אשי אמר מדרישא משיכה אינה קונה
notes.he: לפי מה שרגיל ר"ת לפסוק כר' יוחנן דאמר דבר תורה מעות קונות משום דפסיק רבא בהחולץ (יבמות דף לז.) בכל דוכתא כוותיה היכא דפליג עליה ריש לקיש בר מתלת קשה מכאן דרב אשי דהוא בתרא יותר מרבא סבר כריש לקיש דמשיכה מפורשת מן התורה מדקאמר משיכה בעובד כוכבים לא קני אלמא דדרשינן לעמיתך במשיכה הא לעובד כוכבים בכסף דאי כרבי יוחנן הא אמר לעמיתך בכסף הא לעובד כוכבים במשיכה וי"ל דרב אשי דהכא הדר ביה לגבי אמימר כדמוכח פרק בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (דף עא.) גבי הא דאמר אמימר משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה תדע דהני פרסאי משדרו פרדשני אהדדי ולא הדרי בהו ושקלו וטרו התם רבינא ורב אשי בההיא מילתא ובסוף שמעתא מסקינן ש"מ משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה ש"מ וגם רבינא מקשה התם לרב אשי מדרבי יוחנן לבן נח ולא קא"ל רב אשי רבי יוחנן לטעמיה דאמר דבר תורה מעות קונות ואנא כריש לקיש סבירא לי שמע מינה דרב אשי גופיה כשהיה אומר מתחלה משיכה אינו קונה לאו משום דסבר לה כריש לקיש דלעולם כרבי יוחנן סבירא ליה לפיכך כי הקשה לו מההיא דבן נח לא רצה להקשות מההיא דדבר תורה מעות קונות דלעולם לעמיתך ולעובד כוכבים בכסף ולענין אונאה אתא לעמיתך כמאן דאמר גזל הכנעני אסור דלמאן דאמר גזל הכנעני מותר לא איצטריך כדאמרינן לעיל ואף על גב דאמרינן בהזהב (ב"מ דף מח.) קרא ומתני' מסייע לריש לקיש היינו לכאורה אבל אפשר לשנויי לקרא שפיר אליבא דרבי יוחנן ומתני' דנתנה לבלן מעל הוה מוקמי ליה ר' יוחנן בבלן עובד כוכבים וההיא דנתנה לספר בישראל ולכך מעל אע"ג דלא משך דמעות קונות וא"ת ומאי סייעתא לריש לקיש הא איהו מוקי הך דנתנה לספר בספר עובד כוכבים הכי נמי מצי לאוקומי ההיא דבלן בעובד כוכבים ואור"ת משום דבלן משמע טפי דאיירי בישראל דומיא דנתנה לחבירו דקתני הוא מעל וחבירו לא מעל משמע חבירו ישראל דבר מעילה הוא ודוקא בלן דלא מחסרא משיכה כדמסיים בההיא משנה לפי שאומר לו הרי מרחץ לפניך הכנס ורחוץ אבל ספר דומיא דבלן דהיינו ספר ישראל לא מעל עד דמשיך ולא אמר רבא קרא ומתני' מסייע ליה לריש לקיש לפי שיסבור כמותו תדע דרבא גופיה הוא דפסק כר' יוחנן לגבי ריש לקיש בכל דוכתא בר מתלת וכי תימא שאני הכא דתניא כוותיה והא התם חשיב חדא מילתא דריש לקיש דתניא כוותיה ואי אפשר לומר דהנהו תלתא גרסינהו בהדי הדדי ואכתי איכא טובא דבפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין עז.) גבי גידין שסופן להקשות משמע דדוקא קאמר רבא תני תלת ותו לא והא דפליגי ר' יוחנן וריש לקיש פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טו.) גבי כל הקודם להורגו זכה ותניא כדריש לקיש דהתם אליבא דרבי אליעזר פליגי והלכה כרבנן ופ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף ו:) גבי נשא ונתן דתניא בברייתא כריש לקיש ור' יוחנן סבר כתנא דמתני' גבי הא דתנן לפני חגיהם של עובדי כוכבים אסור לאחריהן מותר ומפרש נשא ונתן איכא בינייהו ומיהו יש לדחות ראיה דרבא כיון דריש לקיש לאו משמיה דנפשיה אמר אלא משום ר' אושעיא כדאמר לעיל אמר ריש לקיש משום רבי אושעיא ישראל שנתן מעות לעובד כוכבים בבהמה בדיניהן ומפרש בדיניהן שפסקה להן תורה מיד עמיתך במשיכה הא לעובד כוכבים בכסף בכי האי גוונא לא איירי רבא לפסוק כר' יוחנן לגבי ריש לקיש בדבר שהיה ריש לקיש אומר בשם רבותיו כדמפרש פ"ב דחולין (דף כט:) בההיא דאין שחיטה אלא לבסוף דאמר ר"ל משום לוי סבא ופליג עליה ר' יוחנן ורבא גופיה סבר כריש לקיש בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים סג.) ובפרק שני דזבחים (דף ל.) ומיהו אשכחן אמר רבא אמר רב הונא מכור לי באלו קנה כו' ומפרש הש"ס דסבר כר' יוחנן דאמר דבר תורה מעות קונות ונראה דרבה גרס ולא רבא דרבא לא ראה רב הונא מעולם דאף רב יהודה לא ראהו כדאמרינן בקדושין (דף עב:) יום שמת רב יהודה נולד רבא וכשמת רב יהודה כבר נפטר רב הונא מדאמר במ"ק (דף יז.) גברא רבא כרב יהודה ליכא דלשרי לך ורב הונא גדול הי' אפילו משמואל רבו של רב יהודה מדאמר בריש גיטין (דף ה.) בעא מיניה שמואל מרב הונא שנים שהביאו גט ועוד יש לדקדק דהלכתא כר' יוחנן דמעות קונות דבר תורה מדאמר וכן אמר רב נחמן דבר תורה מעות קונות ופסק לוי כמתני' וקי"ל כוותיה בדיני והא דאמר פ"ק דקידושין (דף יד:) גבי עבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים עובד כוכבים דכל קניינו בכסף בע"ע קאמר ולא בכל דבר דלר' יוחנן הוי במשיכה והא דמתרץ הש"ס בפרק בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (דף סג.) בזונה עובדת כוכבים דלא מחסרא משיכה ההיא שינוייא כר"ל ולא כר' יוחנן ואידך שינוייא דמשני התם בזונה ישראלית וכגון דקאי בחצירה ניחא אף כר' יוחנן אבל מעיקרא ניחא ליה לאוקומי אפילו לא קאי בחצירה א"נ רב נחמן בר יצחק דקאמר לההיא שינויא דסבירא ליה כר"ל ולא כמו שכתוב בספרים רב חסדא דרב חסדא הוא דאמר פרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מז:) כדרך שתיקנו משיכה בשומרין כך תקנו משיכה בלקוחות אלמא כר' יוחנן סבירא ליה דמשיכה תקנה דרבנן היא ומיהו יש לדחות דאפ"ה כר' יוחנן ס"ל אפשר דהתם דלעובד כוכבים בכסף ולעמיתך ידרוש לענין אונאה כמאן דאמר גזל הכנעני אסור כדפרישית לעיל:
notes.en: In brief: Rabbeinu Tam usually rules like Rabbi Yoḥanan that by Torah law money acquires, since Rava rules in HaḤoletz (Yevamot 36a) that the halakha follows Rabbi Yoḥanan against Reish Lakish everywhere except three cases. This is difficult from here: Rav Ashi, later than Rava, says pulling does not acquire with a gentile, which implies he expounds “your counterpart” by pulling and a gentile with money, as Reish Lakish does. Answer: Rav Ashi retracted in favor of Ameimar, as the last chapter of Avoda Zara (71a) shows: Ameimar’s proof that pulling acquires with a gentile from the Persians, who send gifts to each other and do not retract, is discussed by Ravina and Rav Ashi and accepted. And when Ravina objects there to Rav Ashi from Rabbi Yoḥanan’s ruling about a descendant of Noah, Rav Ashi does not answer that Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own view that money acquires while he himself follows Reish Lakish; so even at first Rav Ashi held like Rabbi Yoḥanan, reading money for both a Jew and a gentile and taking “your counterpart” to teach exploitation, per the view that robbing a gentile is forbidden. As for HaZahav (Bava Metzia 48a), “the verse and the mishna support Reish Lakish”: that is only at first glance; the verse can be read with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who would set the mishna’s bath attendant as a gentile and its barber as a Jew. And if you say Reish Lakish could equally set the bath attendant as a gentile: Rabbeinu Tam answers that “bath attendant” implies a Jew, like “his fellow” in that mishna, and only a bath attendant lacks no pulling (“here is the bathhouse before you, enter and bathe”). Rava did not say “the verse and the mishna support Reish Lakish” because he rules with him, for Rava himself rules with Rabbi Yoḥanan except in three cases. Nor can one say a supporting baraita makes the difference, since one of the three is already a case where a baraita supports Reish Lakish, and Ḥullin (77a), on sinews that will later harden, implies “three and no more”; Sanhedrin (15a) and Avoda Zara (6b), where baraitot support Reish Lakish, are explained otherwise. Yet the proof from Rava can be rejected: here Reish Lakish speaks in the name of Rabbi Oshaya, and Rava does not rule against Reish Lakish where he speaks in his teachers’ name, as in Ḥullin (29b), where Reish Lakish speaks for Levi the Elder and Rava follows him in Pesaḥim (63a) and Zevaḥim (30a). The report “Rava said that Rav Huna said: sell it to me for these [coins], he has acquired” should read Rabba, for Rava never saw Rav Huna: he was born the day Rav Yehuda died (Kiddushin 72b), Rav Huna died before Rav Yehuda (Mo’ed Katan 17a), and Rav Huna was senior even to Shmuel (Gittin 5a). A further proof that the halakha follows Rabbi Yoḥanan: “And so said Rav Naḥman: by Torah law money acquires,” and we follow Rav Naḥman in monetary law. Kiddushin (14b), “a gentile, whose entire acquisition is by money,” refers only to a Hebrew slave. The answer in Avoda Zara (63a) about a gentile prostitute, where pulling is not lacking, follows Reish Lakish; the other answer there, a Jewish prostitute standing in her own courtyard, fits Rabbi Yoḥanan too. Alternatively, that answer is Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak’s, who holds like Reish Lakish, and not Rav Ḥisda’s as the books read, since Rav Ḥisda says in HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b) that the Sages instituted pulling for purchasers, i.e., like Rabbi Yoḥanan; though this too can be rejected, since he could hold like Rabbi Yoḥanan and still read “to your counterpart” as teaching exploitation. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: The baraita is discussing a case where it was agreed that the transaction would be subject to Jewish law. From the fact that in the latter clause, pulling effects acquisition, in the first clause too, pulling effects acquisition.

notes.dh: רבינא אמר מדסיפא משיכה קונה כו'
notes.he: וכגון שקיבל עליו לדון בדיני ישראל. וקסבר האי תנא דאיצטריך למימר דאין צריך לעמוד בדיבורו עם העובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Ravina says: from the latter clause, pulling acquires, etc.: and it is a case where he accepted upon himself to be judged by Jewish law. And this tanna holds that it was necessary to say that one need not keep his word with the gentile.

messages.text: And as for the difficulty with regard to the first clause, which states that the Jew may return the item even though he already pulled it, this is what the baraita is saying: If the buyer did not give the money to the gentile and also did not pull the item, he returns the item to the seller.

notes.dh: ורישא הכי קאמר אם לא נתן מעות כו'
notes.he: פירוש וגם אם לא משך יחזור:
notes.en: And the first clause means this: if he did not give money, etc.: meaning, and also if he did not pull, he may retract.

messages.text: What does the term: Returns, mean in this context? It means that the Jew returns, i.e., reneges, on his verbal commitment. In other words, he is not required to complete the purchase despite the fact he initially agreed to do so.

notes.he: הא לא משך כלום:
notes.en: What is “returns”? But he did not pull anything.

notes.he: ונפדו חייבים בבכורה ומתנות. הזרוע והלחיים והקבה דכיון דמום קדם להקדש ונפדו כחולין דמו:
notes.en: He returns on his words: [retracting] from the terms of the transfer. [The words that follow, “And once redeemed, they are obligated in the firstborn and in the gifts, the foreleg, the jaw and the maw, since a blemish preceded the consecration, and once redeemed they are like non-sacred animals,” gloss the mishna that opens 14a.]

messages.text: It was necessary for the tanna to teach this explicitly, as he holds: Reneging on a verbal commitment that was unaccompanied by an act of acquisition constitutes an act of bad faith between two parties.

notes.dh: דקסבר דברים יש בהן משום מחוסרי אמנה
notes.he: אם חוזר בדיבורו:
notes.en: For he holds that words involve a breach of faith: if he retracts from what he said.

messages.text: And he holds that this statement applies only to a case where a Jew purchases an item from another Jew, as they are assumed to uphold their verbal commitments. But in a case of a Jew who purchases an item from gentiles, as they are not assumed to uphold their verbal commitments, reneging on one’s word does not constitute an act of bad faith between the parties, since neither party relies upon the commitment of the other in the first place.

notes.he: תימה דדומיא דרישא ישראל מעובד כוכבים שמפסיד הכל כגון כאן שמפסיד דמי עבודת כוכבים מי איכא ישראל מישראל משום מחוסרי אמנה וי"ל דהכי קאמר דישראל מעובד כוכבים אי הוה בהו משום מחוסרי אמנה הוה דומה דמי עבודת כוכבים ביד ישראל אע"פ שהוא מקח טעות היה צריך לקיים המקח שלא יהא בו משום מחוסרי אמנה:
notes.en: And this applies to a Jew from a Jew, etc.: This is puzzling: [the case] similar to the first clause, a Jew [buying] from a gentile where he loses everything, as here, where he loses the value of the idol: is there a breach of faith in such a case even between a Jew and a Jew? One can say that this is what it means: with a Jew [buying] from a gentile, if words involved a breach of faith, it would look like the value of idol worship in the possession of a Jew, [for] even though it is a mistaken transaction, he would have to uphold the sale so that there be no breach of faith.

messages.text: 14a opens with a new mishna: sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration.
